title: Global Temperature and Climate Change
seo_title: Grade 6 Climate Change Worksheets: Greenhouse Effect, CO₂ Data and Evidence
standard_text: Ask questions to clarify evidence of the factors that have caused the rise in global temperatures over the past century.
meta_desc: Free middle school science worksheets on global temperature and climate change (NGSS MS-ESS3-5): the greenhouse effect, carbon dioxide and methane, CO₂ and temperature data, and evidence such as melting ice. 100 practice questions with answers.
key_sub: Burning fossil fuels adds carbon dioxide that traps heat. Temperature records, CO₂ data and melting ice are evidence.
body_html:
How to think about it

Earth's average temperature has risen about 1 °C since the late 1800s. Scientists ask questions and gather evidence to find out why.

The greenhouse effect: gases like carbon dioxide (CO₂) and methane trap heat. This keeps Earth livable, but more of these gases trap more heat.

Main human causes: burning fossil fuels (coal, oil, gas), cutting forests and some farming. Evidence: rising temperature records, rising CO₂ measurements, shrinking glaciers and sea ice, and rising sea level.

Example

CO₂ rose from 317 ppm (1960) to 414 ppm (2020). How much?

414 − 317

Answer: 97 ppm

Example

Which helps: planting trees or burning more coal?

Trees take in CO₂.

Answer: planting trees

Common mistakes

  • Thinking the greenhouse effect is always bad. It keeps Earth warm; extra gases cause the problem.
  • Thinking global warming means every day is hotter.
  • Mixing up the ozone hole with global warming.

faq.q: What is causing global temperatures to rise?
faq.a: Mainly greenhouse gases like carbon dioxide from burning fossil fuels, plus cutting forests, which trap more heat in the atmosphere.

faq.q: What evidence shows Earth is warming?
faq.a: Temperature records, rising carbon dioxide measurements, shrinking glaciers and sea ice, and rising sea level.
The natural greenhouse effect keeps Earth warm enough for life. Adding extra greenhouse gases causes extra warming.

items.q: Noah is collecting evidence that Earth's climate is warming. Which is the strongest scientific evidence?
c: My friend says winters used to be colder.
A movie showed a big storm.
It was cold in my town last Tuesday.
Thermometer records show the average global temperature has risen about 1 °C since the late 1800s.
items.e: Strong evidence comes from many measurements over many years, not one day or one opinion.

items.q: Which gases are greenhouse gases?
c: ozone only
helium and neon
carbon dioxide, methane and water vapor
oxygen and nitrogen only
items.e: These gases absorb heat.
